J U D G M E NT /AWAR D 1.
Vide this judgment/award, I shall dispose off DAR filed by IO SI Mohit Chahar, in regard to death of Sh. Rama Shankar, (in short, the deceased), who died in a road vehicular accident on 27.08.2022.

2. Brief facts as per DAR are that on 27.08.2022 deceased was riding on his scooty bearing registration no. DL 4S CW 8047 and at about 07:54 O'clock when deceased reached near Sukhi Nehar, Bara Haridas Talab, Kirari, Delhi, one truck bearing registration no. NL 02 AF 1728 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) hit the scooty of deceased due to which deceased came under the rear wheels of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle i.e. R1 fled away from the spot.
Deceased was shifted to SGM Hospital vide MLC no. 22255/22 where he was declared brought dead.

FIR no. 917/2022 for offence punishable under Section 279/304 A IPC, 146/196 &
66(1)/192A MV Act was registered on the basis of GD entry at PS Aman Vihar.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
